title: Signal Over the South Bay
dek: A jet-age comic in a cover and seven pages: the broadcast station in the sky goes dark before dawn, and a test pilot and an engineer fly out of El Segundo to bring the morning edition home.
author: guest
source: Mike Hoydich's chat request, 2026-10-19: create a future-world comic in a late-1950s/early-60s jet-age adventure style and publish it on PointCast. Publisher: Mike Hoydich. Filed as author guest, as with block 0696, because the author enum has no grok-bot value. Model credits are in meta.guest_byline.
body:
An original jet-age comic for PointCast, in a cover and seven pages.

El Segundo, tomorrow, the way 1962 pictured it. Every morning at 6:45 the Lantern, a broadcast station that floats high above the South Bay, sends the town its paper: weather, tides, swell and news, out to every beach-house radio.

At 4:12 A.M. the Lantern goes dark. Capt. Della Marsh, test pilot for the El Segundo Aero Works, wakes up her rocket-plane, the Gull. Rusty Vance, the engineer who built half of the station's dish, refuses to be left behind.

They find the dish knocked off its mark by a meteor shower and beaming at the moon, and they turn it back toward home by hand. At 6:45 on the dot, the morning edition reaches the beach.

Read all eight images, with a full text transcript of every caption and balloon, at /features/signal-over-the-south-bay/.

The same page also holds Edition B, a portrait pass of the same story, six El Segundo posters, and the brand book. The posters are Block 0734. The brand book is Block 0735.

This is original fiction. The station, the aircraft, the company, and the people are invented.

Guest byline: Grok Bot (script, lettering), Grok Imagine (Edition A art), ChatGPT image generation (Edition B, posters, art), publisher Mike Hoydich.
